title: Second supported coordinate extraction before a trace
statement:
Let A be finite commutative, f:X→Y proper, L∈D_A(Y) with canonical swap(L,L)=id, B∈D_A(X), e:B≅f*L and K∈D_A(Y). Use [def-sf-supported-diagonal-calculus]. Put F=Rf!, H K=B⊗f*K and β2=f*F B≅Rp2!p1*B. Define χ(B,N,K):(B⊗f*K)⊗f*N≅B⊗f*(N⊗K) as the associator, then 1_B tensor swap(f*K,f*N), then the inverse pullback tensor comparison. This is extractionShuffle, with no choice of data. The two maps from Rp2!(p1*(HK)⊗p2*B) to B⊗f*(FB⊗K) agree:
C_B(HK);H(Q_f(B,K)^(-1)) = Rp2!(coordinateTwisted(f,L,K,e)⊗1);π_(p2,HK,p2*B)^(-1);(1_(HK)⊗(Rp2!(coordinate(f,L,e)^(-1));β2^(-1)));χ(B,FB,K).
No scalar trace, diagonal class, integral or triangular identity is assumed.

source.place: Second supported coordinate extraction before a trace; the coordinate triangle computation before applying its scalar trace

proof.text: Use the native right-coefficient compact projection/exchange identity projectionMap_rightDerivedLowerShriekBaseChangeMap for the canonical self-product square. Combine the pullback tensor comparison and inverse square comparison as coefficientSplit. Invert the exchange and projection isomorphisms by cancellation. This directly proves inverse_exchange, without passing through ordinary direct images or forget-supports comparisons. The compact operations are those of def-amb-etale-compact-support.

Tensor the inverted square with B. Apply projectionMapAssociativity (lem-route-projection-map-associativity), naturality in the base coefficient, braidedness of pullback, and the symmetric monoidal hexagons. The resulting cyclic_projection identity, specialized as projection_cycle, replaces successive inverse projections by the inverse ordered projection and cyclicShuffle.

Apply lem-sf-supported-coefficient-braid: coefficientSplit tensored with p2*B followed by cyclicShuffle equals coordinateTwisted tensored with p2*B followed by the inverse coordinate comparison on B. This is the common coefficient and even-symmetry calculation, involving only inverse images and tensor products.

Move the remaining inverse coordinate comparison through inverse ordered projection by naturality. Move inverse exchange on B through the associator and symmetry by naturality. The final three maps are exactly extractionShuffle. Expanding comparison at the start gives the required equality with the original canonical maps. These cancellations take place before any scalar trace or diagonal class is supplied. Generic tensor component equations and the component equations for composite functors identify the raw derived-functor presentation with the monoidal diagram chase, without changing any canonical map.

lean.statement:
theorem secondExtraction {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (L : DerivedCategoryModule A Y)
    (hL : (CoordinateTrace.swap A Y L L).hom = 𝟙 _)
    {B : DerivedCategoryModule A X} (e : B ≅ (CoordinateTrace.pull A f).obj L)
    (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y) :
    (comparison A f B
        (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).obj
          ((CoordinateTrace.pull A f).obj K))).hom ≫
        ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).map
          ((CoordinateTrace.pull A f).map ((projectionIso A f B).inv.app K)) =
      (push A (pullback.snd f f)).map
          (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (pullback f f)).map
            (coordinateTwisted A f L K e).hom).app
              ((CoordinateTrace.pull A (pullback.snd f f)).obj B)) ≫
        (orderedProjection A (pullback.snd f f)
          (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).obj
            ((CoordinateTrace.pull A f).obj K))
          ((CoordinateTrace.pull A (pullback.snd f f)).obj B)).inv ≫
        ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj
          (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).obj
            ((CoordinateTrace.pull A f).obj K))).map
          ((push A (pullback.snd f f)).map (SfDiagonalKernel.coordinate A f L e).inv ≫
            (TraceDiagonalDatum.baseChangeIso (Λ := A) f).inv.app B) ≫
        (extractionShuffle (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f B ((push A f).obj B) K).hom
